performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body:
@Negabinary I broke out dynamics / incremental eval related fixes / changes below (claudeslop but edited for correctness), lmk if anything smells to you.

## Incremental-eval staleness fix (the ∅-until-next-edit bug)
- **`src/web/app/editors/code/CodeWithStatics.re`** — placing a probe (or autoprobe) showed the empty-set indicator until the next edit: the statics debounce left per-id `probe_targets` stale, so `IncrEval.reuse_check` matched the cached entry and reused a state slice with no sample for the new probe. Fix: force a full statics re-init when the zipper's probe ids differ from the cached targets (bypassing the debounce). Closes #2323/#2276.

## Eval state slice now carries call frames
- **`src/language/dynamics/state/StateSlice.re`** — the incremental-eval state slice's `app_data` is now `Id.Map.t(list((call_stack, elided_value, stack_frame)))` (was `app_args`, a 2-tuple with no frame); `diff_app_args` → `diff_app_data` retyped. Changes what's diffed / carried across incremental eval. This data was necessary for step-into to work properly for indirect function calls (eg function passed as param).
- **`src/language/dynamics/state/EvaluatorState.re`** — `app_args`→`app_data` rename + frame storage; `lookup_app_arg`→`lookup_app` merged (returns `(elided_value, stack_frame)`). `clear_transient` still wipes it before postMessage.

## Transition / Evaluator (step-into for indirect calls)
- **`src/language/dynamics/transition/Transition.re`** — step-into through a function **cast** now builds the inner `Ap` with `rewrap` (reuse the redex id) instead of `fresh`, so the call keeps identity across the cast; partial-application (`DeferredAp`) steps now emit `RecordStackFrame`; `get_fn_name`/`get_fn_def_id` made recursive through `Closure`/`DeferredAp`.
- **`src/language/dynamics/Evaluator.re`** — the probe-on-`Ap` path looks up `(args, frame)` via `lookup_app` and carries `~frame` into `Sample.mk`.

## Sample identity / ordering
- **`src/language/dynamics/Sample.re`** — sample-id collision hardening: `Hashtbl.hash_param(64, 256, (List.length(stack), syntax_id, stack))` (cheap discriminators first) replaces `Hashtbl.hash`, fixing collisions on deep recursive stacks sharing a prefix.

> Incremental-eval staleness fix (the ∅-until-next-edit bug)

This is the right fix - I think I saw this on a separate pr 

> Eval state slice now carries call frames

Concerns me greatly and doesn't feel like it should be a thing, though it will be made redundant by #2339 anyway so I guess we can keep it to fix whatever Claude thought it was fixing with that

> step-into through a function cast now builds the inner Ap with rewrap

uh probably harmless but I wanna know why - and whether this suggests we need to document a new invariant in transition, notably it goes against the comment already in Transition.re

```
  /* Note[Matt]: For IDs, I'm currently using a fresh id
     if anything about the current node changes, if only its
     children change, we use rewrap */
```

Asking Claude this question reassured me a little that this might actually be just for one very specific circumstance.

> partial-application (DeferredAp) steps now emit RecordStackFrame

seems reasonable

Rich probes/tables rendering is broken if you use the inline view. I'd also be okay to switch to something closer to the version I have in https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/tree/resizable-probe-modal which replaces the sample with the rich version if that's easier. Also the vertical scrolling for tall inline samples doesn't have any visual indicator that it's scrollable.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4f51691-58c4-43c2-b7ff-a6382a81ec15
@7h3kk1d both are fixed. in drawer mode, just the table display is used
